title: Safety-margin autotuner for interleaved prefill/decode kernel selection
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: On mixed workloads where prefill (long-context) and decode (short/streamed) requests are interleaved, our kernel selector frequently oscillates between high-throughput kernels optimized for long seq-len and low-latency kernels for short seq-len. This causes tail latency spikes and additional KV-cache/prefill warmup costs when kernel handoffs happen mid-session.

Goal: Implement a kernel autotuner that (1) uses a compact safety-margin buffer on top of the estimated latency/cost model to prefer stable kernels across transient seq-len shifts, (2) blends offline microbenchmark profiles with light-weight online probes, and (3) exposes a controlled rollout with feature flags and telemetry for evaluating tail-latency and cost trade-offs. Target SLO: reduce 95th-percentile latency regressions caused by kernel handoffs by >=30% on mixed traffic without increasing median token cost by more than 5%.

Approach:
- Build a "safety margin" parameter (adaptive per GPU family) added to the cost/latency comparator so a new kernel must beat the incumbent by margin M (ms or relative %) before an immediate handoff.
- Compute M as combination of an architecture baseline (offline microbench) and a traffic-adaptive term derived from recent tail quantiles (online moving window).
- Use a two-stage autotune: (A) offline sweep over candidate kernels across seq-len buckets and hardware types (existing microbench harness), (B) lightweight online probes (small percentage of requests or synthetic probe traffic) to calibrate margin and detect drift.
- Add hysteresis for prefills: if a prefill is ongoing and the new kernel would force an expensive cache flush/warmup, increase margin temporarily to avoid unnecessary swaps.
- Provide per-customer config knobs (safety_margin_ms, probe_fraction, exp_backoff) and a global opt-in feature flag for incremental rollout.

Why different from prior work: many autotuners pick the statistically optimal kernel per bucket but lack an explicit stability objective tied to prefill warmup cost and tail-latency impact. The safety-margin concept makes stability a first-class constraint and reduces oscillation in mixed workloads.

Success metrics and telemetry:
- 95th and 99th latency delta (per model, per route) vs baseline when traffic mixes prefill/decode at ratios 20/80, 50/50, 80/20.
- Number of kernel switches per 1k requests (should decrease).
- Token-cost delta and GPU utilization.
- Prefill cache hit ratio and warmup time after handoffs.
- Regression alerts if generation quality or correctness changes (sanity checks).
acceptance_criteria: Implement safety-margin aggregator that combines offline per-arch baseline with an online tail-quantile term
Expose configuration (safety_margin_ms, probe_fraction, backoff_policy) and feature-flag gating in runtime config
Run offline microbench sweep and produce candidate margins for current supported GPU families; store in kernel-catalog metadata
Ship lightweight online probe harness that can be toggled per-route and collects latency/cost impact metrics
Show proof-of-concept canary in staging with 50k mixed-workload requests demonstrating >=30% improvement in 95th latency vs baseline in at least two models
Guardrails: rollout defaults that do not increase median token cost by >5% and include automatic rollback on QoS regressions
